title: The Solar System
subtitle: The Sun to Pluto
sourceNote: Semi-major axes from the NASA planetary fact sheets.

waypoints.name: Mercury
waypoints.body: The smallest planet and the fastest. A year here lasts 88 days. The day side reaches 430 degrees, the night side minus 180.

waypoints.name: Venus
waypoints.body: Earth's twin in size and nothing like it otherwise. Ninety atmospheres of pressure, clouds of sulphuric acid, and 464 degrees at the surface.

waypoints.name: Earth
waypoints.body: One astronomical unit, by definition. Sunlight takes eight minutes and twenty seconds to get here. You are already past home.

waypoints.name: Mars
waypoints.body: The last of the rocky planets — and that is all four of them, inside the first four percent of your route.

waypoints.name: Ceres and the asteroid belt
waypoints.body: Mostly empty. If you flew straight through the belt you would be unlikely to see a single asteroid.

waypoints.name: Jupiter
waypoints.body: Two and a half times the mass of every other planet combined. The Great Red Spot has been turning for at least three hundred years.

waypoints.name: Saturn
waypoints.body: The rings are two hundred and eighty thousand kilometres across and only about ten metres thick.

waypoints.name: Uranus
waypoints.body: Tipped over on its side by ninety-eight degrees. Each pole gets forty-two years of continuous sunlight, then forty-two years of dark. Almost exactly the midpoint of your route.

waypoints.name: Neptune
waypoints.body: Winds of two thousand kilometres per hour, the fastest in the solar system. Sunlight here is nine hundred times dimmer than on Earth.

waypoints.name: Pluto
waypoints.body: You have arrived. New Horizons took nine and a half years to make this trip. From here the Sun is just the brightest star in the sky.
